milestone: Brownie MCP Runtime Safety Policy Finite Closure

strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Requires MCP stdio execution to bind the trusted Mode Pack executable to Runtime-owned bounded content identity before launch without turning executable identity into authority.
Allows autonomous runs to detect executable drift between task-pinned catalog admission and later tools/call execution without relying on human inspection or external wrapper checks.
Keeps MCP tool execution request-scoped, provenance-bound, and fail-closed when the executable target changes or is invalid before spawn.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances runtime_permission_enforcement, headless_autonomous_development, and controlled_workspace_tools by adding Runtime-owned executable identity admission and launch rechecks for MCP stdio servers.
answers.new_capability: Runtime can pin the executable identity used to build an MCP tool catalog and fail closed if the executable is missing, non-regular, unreadable, oversized, drifting, or mismatched before tools/list or tools/call spawn.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: Before MCP-S7, Brownie required an absolute command, denied PATH lookup, cleared environment, and used a neutral cwd, but it did not bind the executable content identity to task-pinned MCP catalog provenance.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: A trusted absolute executable path could change after catalog materialization without explicit Runtime drift evidence, weakening task-pinned MCP provenance before release.
answers.non_duplicative: This phase changes Runtime MCP launch admission, catalog provenance, task-pinned catalog matching, execution metadata, specs, and audits; it is not a wrapper, report, registry, signing system, package manager, or documentation-only verdict.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The existing tools/list, tool.execute, task.run, and headless run/resume boundaries are preserved; executable identity is Runtime launch-boundary evidence below those surfaces.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The phase updates existing execution behavior and bounded evidence rather than adding a report, readiness endpoint, or diagnostic wrapper.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Runtime hashes executable content before tools/list, records only bounded identity fingerprints, rechecks identity before tools/list and tools/call spawn, and denies drift or invalid executable targets before server execution.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Headless runs can rely on task-pinned MCP executable provenance and fail closed during resume or later tool execution if the server binary changed after admission.
answers.milestone_progress: Closes MCP-S7, the final MCP Runtime Safety Policy phase, while Runtime Release Ready remains false until other recorded Runtime Release Readiness P0/P1 blockers are closed.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: MCP-S7 changes Runtime MCP stdio launch behavior and Runtime release audit state, so strict review must verify executable identity remains narrowing-only, fail-closed, and never persists raw paths, command strings, or binary content.

exit_criteria: Runtime computes bounded executable content identity for MCP stdio server config without ledgering raw executable content, raw command strings, absolute paths, or canonical paths.
Task-pinned MCP catalog evidence carries bounded executable identity fingerprints and catalog fingerprints cover executable identity.
tools/list and tools/call recheck executable identity immediately before stdio spawn.
Missing, non-regular, unreadable, oversized, drifting, or mismatched executables fail closed before spawn.

Executable identity cannot override Mode Pack allow-lists, mcp_tool_access, S2 safety policy, S3 annotations, S4 approval binding, S5 schema validation, S6 secret references, catalog drift, or Runtime authority.
MCP-S7 is marked closed while Runtime Release Ready remains false until the other recorded Runtime Release Readiness P0/P1 blockers are closed.
behavior_evidence: brownie-runtime focused test coverage proves executable identity is cataloged without raw path evidence.
brownie-runtime focused test coverage proves executable drift after catalog admission fails closed before tools/call spawn.
brownie-runtime focused test coverage proves non-regular executable targets fail before spawn.
docs/architecture/mcp-runtime-safety-policy-audit.json records MCP-S7 as closed and removes MCP-specific release blockers while Runtime Release Ready remains false.

accepted_capability: MCP stdio executable identity is Runtime-pinned, task-pinned, and rechecked before launch.
MCP Runtime Safety Policy S1 through S7 are implemented sufficiently for stdio MCP safety closure.
behavior_evidence: Runtime focused test coverage proves bounded executable identity provenance, drift denial before spawn, and invalid executable denial before spawn.
safety_boundary: Rust Runtime remains the execution, admission, replay, permission, tool, workspace mutation, and completion authority.
Mode Pack structured policy remains the MCP tool safety authority; MCP executable identity, secret references, schemas, annotations, descriptions, results, and model output cannot grant authority.

Executable identity can only narrow or deny launch; it cannot widen Mode Pack policy, allow-list membership, approval binding, annotations, schema validation, secret resolution, or catalog provenance.
non_goals: Does not add PATH lookup, package installation, remote fetch, registry lookup, signing infrastructure, binary provenance systems, or remote binary distribution.
Does not add Streamable HTTP, OAuth, MCP Apps, Sampling, Roots, Elicitation, hosted secret manager, or public registry.
Does not add a Brownie-specific tool adapter SDK or protocol.
Does not add scheduler, daemon, generic shell, arbitrary process execution, recursive Brownie invocation, hosted platform, forge adapters, or remote Git expansion.
Does not close the remaining non-MCP Runtime Release Readiness P0/P1 blockers.
rejected_alternatives: Rejected raw path or canonical path persistence because durable evidence must remain bounded and path-free.
Rejected raw executable content persistence because binary content must not enter ledger, prompts, diagnostics, or control-plane documents.
Rejected external signing, registry, package manager, and remote binary provenance systems because MCP-S7 is limited to Runtime-owned v0 content identity checks.
Rejected CLI-owned executable validation because Runtime owns MCP launch, evidence, replay, and permission boundaries.
technical_debt: Previously recorded Runtime Release Readiness blockers remain open, including boundary protocol contracts, explicit cancel command, real process-loss recovery E2E, durable schema version and migration, full CI workflow hardening, protocol/event canonization, runtime module decomposition reevaluation, and platform/deadline/durability hardening.
Owner license/publish decision remains required before OSS release basis can be claimed.

runtime_release_dod: Runtime-owned MCP permission checks, tool execution, bounded evidence, replay, completion semantics, request-scoped stdio launch, secret references, and executable identity checks.

Task-pinned Mode Pack policy, catalog provenance, annotation provenance, approval provenance, schema provenance, secret reference fingerprints, executable identity fingerprints, and point-of-use Runtime safety enforcement.

external_adapter_responsibilities: MCP server implementation, GitHub/GitLab/Slack adapters, OAuth application wiring, remote transport hosting, hosted credential management, registries, signing infrastructure, and package distribution.
